The largest flat agricultural valleys in Greece are near Thessaloniki and Larissa. Smaller flat valleys, with mountains appearing closer, are found in other parts of the north and center.
Aleppo pine grows across Central Greece and is typical in Attica and northern Euboea. It's also common in the Chalkidiki "fingers." Unlike Brutia pine, Aleppo often forms dense forests.
Alexandreia uses bins with Alexander the Great on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city
Argos uses bins with this design on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city
Yellow taxis are found in Athens.

On many of the central islands you can find a very

  • barren landscape
  • small bushes
  • no trees in sight This tends to be more common on the smaller islands with coverage.
Chalkiadakis supermarkets are unique to Crete. NOTE: On the stores there is not always a logo (only text).
Full dark blue taxis are found in Chania.
Mastic trees are very common in the southern part of the Chios island.
Citrus plantations are mainly found in coastal areas, particularly on southern Peloponnese.
On Crete, you may find this unique car antenna, with a slight bulge at the tip.
CRM Supermarkets can be seen in Macedonia and on Crete. Together with landscape this can be a useful clue.

One of the most well-known types of Greek architecture; houses with

  • completely white walls
  • blue doors
  • and shutters Is mainly found on the small central Cyclade islands.
Grey stone houses with slate roofs are typical for Epirus, especially around Vikos Gorge in Pindus National Park. Even single grey stone houses are a good hint for this region.
Unlike the Northern Pindus, in the Southern half of the Pindus range, fir trees are the dominant species.
A road from Kilkis to Kerkini Lake National Park (north of Thessaloniki) features French-style bollards, which are unique in Greece. Look at the map for exact locs.
Large clusters of plastic greenhouses are common and effective in the Ierapetra area of southeastern Crete. Smaller greenhouse clusters also appear along other parts of Crete's southern coast.
Heraklion uses bins with a griffin on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city
"Jetoil" gas stations are only seen in northern Greece. website with exact locs
Alexandreia uses bins with a sticker with 2 flowers on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city
Kos uses bins with a Tree or Flower on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city
Limnos has a unique, green landscape with few trees, many yellow flowers (likely dark mullein), and dense low bushes on hills.
Within the Decentralised Administration of Macedonia and Thrace you will sometimes find these alternative bollards.
On the Mani peninsula in the Peloponnese you’ll find these unique stone towerhouses.
These extraordinary monolithic mountains are called Meteora, and can be found north of Trikala.
Mount Pangaion stands out as a solitary mountain rather than part of a wide range and is located just south of a flat agricultural valley.
Mykonos uses bins with this design on them (also you can read "MYKONOY"). NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins on the Island
Naousa uses bins with a logo on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city
Olive plantations are found in coastal areas, particularly on Crete and southern Peloponnese.
Patras uses bins with a sticker on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city
Patras uses (dark)-red taxis.
Greece is the world’s 3rd largest producer of peaches, and these are heavily concentrated around the cities of Edessa and Veria, along with some other non-citrus fruit plantations.
While the map shows several hotspots, the main areas with Pinus Nigra forests are at the northern end of the Pindus Mountains. The spots in the Peloponnese are also notable.
The island of Egina is full of pistacchio plantations, which are relatively unique to the island.
Rice can only be seen in these two areas
Heraklion is a popular holiday spot for Russians, and it is not uncommon to find signs written in Russian in the more touristic parts.
Santorini architecture is very distinct. Like cyclade architecture more generally, it is very whitewashed, however it is distinct for its curved roofs and semi-circle windows/porticoes.
Some houses on Ikaria have these distinct roofs made of large slate slabs.
Sunflower plantations are most common in the far northeast corner of the country and generally restricted to the north of the country.
Synka supermarkets are unique to Crete (especially west).
The tallest Greek mountains are found in the western half of the country, and contain most of the country’s high-altitude mountain roads with coverage.
In Thessaloniki, you will often see a large amount of unusually tall antennas on top of buildings.
Alexandreia uses bins with stylised thetas (θ)** on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city
Blue taxis with a white roof are found in Thessaloniki.
Veria uses bins with two coins on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city
Volos uses bins with a ship and the greek name ("Βόλος") on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city
